question: does the broker route change the accepted R7 interpreter/package identity, and what requalification burden follows?

does_the_broker_route_require_a_rebuild_.finding: the file-object route already exists in the accepted 1.3.6 build; it is reached by passing a file-like object instead of a path. No recompilation, no dyld interposition, no root, no SIP change.
does_the_broker_route_require_a_rebuild_.contrast_with_the_previously_failed_appr: the HQ194/HQ191 attempts (DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES, __DATA,__interpose) failed; this route does not depend on either

does_the_broker_route_change_executed_ru.semantic_change_to_reader_output: NONE OBSERVED on synthetic carriers — the returned frame, columns and row counts were identical between the path route and the broker route
does_the_broker_route_change_executed_ru.physical_change: YES — the byte source changes from the compiled reader's internal I/O to the Python bridge, which is precisely what makes the literal account observable
does_the_broker_route_change_executed_ru.assessment: this is an I/O-path substitution that preserves decoded results on synthetic carriers, but it is NOT nothing: it moves the read boundary into Python and therefore changes the performance and failure surface

requalification_effect.identity_spine: UNCHANGED — the R7 interpreter and package versions are untouched; no re-provisioning is implicated
what_still_requires_requalification: source-free equivalence at the prior court grain: path route vs broker route must be shown to produce identical decoded results across the full source-free corpus (the HQ196 adjudication lists this as outstanding proof item 6; this review verified it only on synthetic carriers)
the premature-EOF ceiling pattern must be re-validated per format, since it relies on ReadStat detecting a short read rather than on a documented guarantee
any pyreadstat version change invalidates the seam: the empty-path convention, the no-op open handler and the bare-except read handler are implementation details
requalification_effect.pinning_requirement: pin pyreadstat to the exact 1.3.6 build (extension sha 7700fb3e...) and re-run the seam checks on any change. The seam is public in its TYPING but private in its BEHAVIOUR.

seam_publicness.evidence: pyreadstat.py exports `class FileLike(Protocol)` with the docstring 'Should work with any file-like object that has read and seek methods'; the read functions' parameter docstring names 'path to the file or file-like object'
but_private_in_behaviour: pyobject_read_handler's BARE except returning -1 (the hang hazard)
seam_publicness.conclusion: not a de-facto private hook the way dyld interposition was, but also not a stability-guaranteed contract. Treat as version-pinned behaviour.
